title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Lanthanide doping of titanium oxo clusters can improve both stability and photoelectrocatalytic water oxidation relative to undoped clusters, with activity tracking the band gap and being highest for variable-valent Eu.
explanation: For isomorphic Ln8Ti10 clusters the review lists coordinated water and cluster oxygen as assisting the rate-limiting first O–H cleavage, a red-shifted gap that increases UV–vis absorption, and a higher activity for Eu8Ti10 than for Sm8Ti10 or Gd8Ti10 because the structures are otherwise isomorphic.
scope: Lanthanide-doped titanium oxo clusters used as molecular models of TiO2 water-oxidation catalysts.
conditions: Eu8Ti10: 500 W mercury lamp, 0.2 M NaAc/AcOH, pH 6.0, ITO electrode; reported TON 7581 and TOF 2527 s−1.
caveats: Transition-metal doping is separately said to narrow the gap of titanium oxo clusters; the Eu advantage is within this isomorphic Ln series, not a universal ranking of all dopants.
